_what: Links a person saved somewhere else, kept in their Trillion files, read by src/saved-links.mjs. Each place they come from is one row: `browser_files` are a browser's own saved-items file the person (or their AI, or Trillion on their computer) hands in, decoded by the shape its row describes; `service_lists` are lists a connected service keeps, read through that service's Workshop tools page by page. Every place's links land in `folder`, one file per group (`file_name`), as JSON: { saved_from, group, updated_at, links: [{ title, url, folder?, saved_at?, key?, ... }] }. Adding a browser or a service is one row here and, for a service, its tools in parts/service-connections/records.json; nothing in the code names one.

arc-sidebar.label: Arc
arc-sidebar.about: Arc keeps every space's pinned tabs and folders, and the favorites along the top, in one file on the Mac: ~/Library/Application Support/Arc/StorableSidebar.json. Its lists alternate a key and its value. The tabs under Today are open tabs, not saved ones, so only pinned items and favorites are kept.

x-bookmarks.label: X
x-bookmarks.about: X lists a person's bookmarks newest first, 100 to a page, and keeps no time a bookmark was made, so the newest one Trillion has seen is where the next read stops. X hands out at most the 800 most recent.

tool.title: Save my X bookmarks
tool.description: Saves this person's X (Twitter) bookmarks into their Trillion files (/Saved links/X - Bookmarks.json, newest first), keeping every one already saved. Leave since out to save every bookmark X hands out (its newest 800); give since, the newest id a read returned, to save only the ones made after it and get them back as items. Trillion also does this by itself every 30 minutes once X is connected, handing each new bookmark to the person's rules. Needs X connected on the Connections screen; list_connections says whether it is.
tool.since: The newest bookmark id an earlier read returned

x-likes.label: X
x-likes.about: X lists the posts a person liked newest first, 100 to a page, and keeps no time a like was made, so the newest one Trillion has seen is where the next read stops.

Leave since out to save every like X hands out; give since, the newest id a read returned, to save only the ones liked after it and get them back as items. Trillion also does this by itself every 30 minutes once X is connected, handing each new like to the person's rules. Needs X connected on the Connections screen with likes allowed; list_connections says whether it is.

url_providers._what: Which place a pasted address belongs to: one row per provider, found by the address's host (the host itself or any name under it). `connection` is the vendor of its service-connection record in parts/service-connections/records.json, which is the one home of how it signs in: the token exchange happens on the server with the sealed client values, and only the NAMES of those values are ever read here. `lists` are the `service_lists` ids that provider can be read through. A provider with no row is not read yet; adding one is a row, once its connection and tools exist.
